svg.title: The three-part test for whether a sub-task should be isolated
svg.desc: A hand-drawn figure. Three cards across the top give the three things a clean contract requires at once: the input is fully specified so the child never asks a clarifying question, the output is structured and finite rather than a conversation, and the work is self-contained with no ongoing access to the parent's evolving state. Below, five example tasks are each given a verdict. Finding three relevant papers, summarising a two hundred page contract, and running a test suite all pass, because the input is clear, the output is small and structured, and the bulk never needs to enter the parent context. Thinking through an architecture fails, because there is no clean output contract and the value is the conversation. Deciding whether to escalate a ticket is borderline: yes if the rules are documented, no if it needs the parent's state. A caption warns that a sub-task failing the test is not rescued by prompt engineering.
svg.text: Isolate when the contract is clean. Otherwise do not.
A clean contract is three things at once, and a sub-task that fails the test is not rescued by prompt engineering.
1 · The input is fully specified
The child never needs to ask
the parent a clarifying question.
2 · The output is finite
A JSON object, a list of
titles, a number. Never "a conversation".
3 · The work is self-contained
It needs no ongoing access to
the parent's evolving state.
Find the three most relevant papers, return titles and DOIs
Yes
Input clear, output structured, self-contained.
Read this 200-page contract and return a summary
Yes
The source never needs to enter the parent context.
Run the test suite, return pass/fail and the failing names
Yes
Enormous tool result, small structured output.
Help me think through the architecture of this feature
No
No output contract; the value is the talk.
Decide whether to escalate this ticket
Borderline
Yes if the rules are written down; no otherwise.
Fail the test and prompt engineering will not rescue it: a chatty child needs context the parent must reload, so you pay twice for a worse answer.
